title: Productive AI tools spread beyond early adopters
mechanism: A verified commercial diffusion improves output per worker; adoption investment and expected incomes raise demand before the full cost reduction arrives. Displacement remains uncertain.
policy_dilemma: Higher supply and investment demand can justify a different stance than either pure boom or slump.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable innovation combines investment, capacity and unit-cost timing without claiming an estimated AI effect.

title: A major producer restricts fertilizer exports
mechanism: Foreign export restrictions raise planting input costs; farms reduce application or absorb lower margins, with food supply pressure arriving after the input-price jump.
policy_dilemma: A delayed harvest effect can outlast the immediate input shock; monetary tightening cannot reopen foreign exports.
selection_reason: Accepted: A lagged input-to-harvest shock differs from weather destroying the current crop.

title: External tariff increases raise imported input costs
mechanism: The elected government imposes an unexpected tariff on widely used intermediate goods; firms pay more before substitution or domestic sourcing expands.
policy_dilemma: Inflation rises while production weakens; the Chair cannot repeal a tariff or presume instant substitution.
selection_reason: Accepted: A nonmonetary policy event tests cost pass-through and supply limits without assigning fiscal/trade powers to the player.

title: Office demand shifts cause commercial-property loan losses
mechanism: External work-location preferences reduce office rental cash flow; exposed loans deteriorate and banks tighten credit even without a deposit run. Liquidity does not repair the loss.
policy_dilemma: Support aggregate demand while recognizing that secured cash cannot create bank capital or viable tenants.
selection_reason: Accepted: A persistent loss wedge without funding need makes the liquidity-versus-capital distinction explicit.

title: Foreign producers unexpectedly cut oil supply
mechanism: Coordinated foreign output cuts raise fuel costs and reduce household purchasing power; spare capacity determines how quickly supply can respond.
policy_dilemma: Balance headline inflation against weaker spending; rate increases cannot create oil.
selection_reason: Accepted: A familiar adverse supply event gives a strong inflation/activity conflict without assigning the Chair energy powers.

title: A new epidemic deters face-to-face spending
mechanism: A contagious outbreak causes voluntary avoidance of travel and crowded services while illness reduces available work; reopening later produces a demand rebound.
policy_dilemma: Weak spending and impaired supply coexist; easier money cannot remove infection risk.
selection_reason: Accepted: Combines a large demand interruption with supply limits and an explicit reopening phase.

title: Attacks force commercial shipping onto longer routes
mechanism: Security threats cause merchant ships to detour, consuming fuel and tying up cargo capacity; deliveries slow and working inventories shrink.
policy_dilemma: Higher imported costs coexist with weak production; the Chair cannot reopen a sea lane.
selection_reason: Accepted: Security-driven rerouting has a clear duration and cost channel, unlike a generic demand slowdown.

title: Uninsured depositors run from otherwise sound banks
mechanism: Confidence news triggers fast withdrawals at otherwise sound depository banks with pledged assets; cash needs rise without an assumed new capital loss. Eligibility is scenario supplied.
policy_dilemma: Use eligible secured lending for funding, not indiscriminate rate cuts; collateral limits still bind.
selection_reason: Accepted: The pure funding case cleanly tests liquidity versus stance and requires no invented bank recapitalization.

title: Avian influenza removes egg-laying flocks
mechanism: Flock culling cuts egg supply rapidly; biological repopulation delays recovery even after transmission subsides. The aggregate pulse is smaller than the grain event.
policy_dilemma: Avoid overreacting to one food category while checking whether expectations spread the price shock.
selection_reason: Accepted: Recognizable biological supply loss has a slower replenishment path and a narrow-price-versus-broad-policy dilemma.

title: Canal water scarcity cuts daily vessel transits
mechanism: Low freshwater availability limits lock operations and draft, forcing shippers to split cargo or choose longer routes; rainfall gradually restores throughput.
policy_dilemma: Transit scarcity raises costs even without more orders; monetary tightening cannot replenish canal water.
selection_reason: Accepted: A capacity constraint tied to lock water differs physically from security-driven detours and remains legible in the reduced form.

title: Severe influenza raises worker absenteeism
mechanism: A severe flu season removes working days without a broad mandatory shutdown; production costs rise while sick households postpone some purchases.
policy_dilemma: Respond to persistent inflation pressure without treating short-lived absenteeism as permanent slack.
selection_reason: Accepted: A health-driven labor-hours shock differs from voluntary avoidance of services.

title: Cyberattack stops a fuel pipeline
mechanism: A commercial pipeline operator suspends distribution, creating regional fuel shortages and precautionary purchases; reopening reverses part of the cost pressure.
policy_dilemma: Resist interpreting panic fuel purchases as durable demand or liquidity as a repair tool.
selection_reason: Accepted: Short physical interruption and purchase payback make the event different from persistent foreign production cuts.

title: Cold snap exhausts readily deliverable gas storage
mechanism: Heating demand surges while gas withdrawal and transport limits bind; factories face higher bills and some curtailment before warmer conditions ease pressure.
policy_dilemma: Heating demand and industrial weakness coexist; choose a response that survives the weather reversal.
selection_reason: Accepted: Demand for essential heating meets a delivery constraint, producing a different energy dilemma from pipeline damage.

title: Drought sharply reduces grain yields
mechanism: Water stress during a critical growing stage lowers the harvest, raises food/feed costs and squeezes farm income; later planting offers only partial relief.
policy_dilemma: Food inflation and weaker real spending pull policy in opposite directions; rates cannot grow crops.
selection_reason: Accepted: Broad grain and feed transmission makes a familiar food supply shock with a clear monetary limit.

title: Extreme heat shortens outdoor shifts
mechanism: Unsafe heat cuts construction and field-work hours without destroying factories; cooler conditions release deferred work. Temporary growth slowing proxies lost productive time.
policy_dilemma: Inflation pressure accompanies weaker capacity; avoid treating fewer hours as a demand collapse.
selection_reason: Accepted: A recognizable productivity interruption tests supply diagnosis without requiring a bank crisis.

title: Ransomware disrupts a shared commercial cloud
mechanism: A concentrated cloud provider outage disables ordering and business applications across otherwise sound firms; restoration releases postponed transactions but lost work remains.
policy_dilemma: Monetary accommodation cannot repair systems; avoid interpreting transaction disruption as vanished final demand.
selection_reason: Accepted: Digital concentration transmits an operational shock broadly without requiring a fabricated solvency loss.

title: A labor dispute stops vehicle assembly
mechanism: A private wage-contract dispute shuts assembly plants and delays supplier orders; settlement restores production and permits a partial backlog rebound. Wage settlement itself is not separately modeled.
policy_dilemma: Lost output and scarce vehicles are supply pressure; monetary policy cannot settle the contract.
selection_reason: Accepted: A production stoppage driven by bargaining differs from unavailable chips and has a concrete negotiated restart.

title: Payment processing failure creates temporary bank cash needs
mechanism: A commercial payment outage delays incoming settlements while outgoing commitments remain; eligible banks need a bridge against already pledged collateral. The quarterly profile aggregates a shorter operational incident.
policy_dilemma: Provide only eligible secured liquidity; systems restoration and final settlement, not lending, resolve the operational cause.
selection_reason: Accepted: A cash-timing failure without assumed insolvency adds a different origin and short unwind to funding stress.

title: Cattle liquidation brings cheap beef before scarcity
mechanism: Forage shortage prompts herd sales, temporarily increasing slaughter supply; a smaller breeding herd subsequently limits beef production. Recovery exceeds the four-quarter input window.
policy_dilemma: Initial food disinflation can conceal later supply scarcity; avoid extrapolating the first quarter.
selection_reason: Accepted: The biological sign reversal creates a strong sequencing problem that a generic food-price increase would miss.

title: Accounting fraud reveals missing corporate borrower earnings
mechanism: A large borrower restates fabricated earnings, defaults on debt and reduces spending; creditors recognize impairment and reassess related lending. This is not caused by the player rate.
policy_dilemma: Lower financing costs cannot restore missing cash flow or cancel realized creditor losses.
selection_reason: Accepted: An external borrower-information shock separates credit losses from cash withdrawal pressure; aggregate size is fictional.

title: Private repo lenders raise dealer collateral haircuts
mechanism: Private repo lenders demand more cash against securities held by dealers after external volatility news; dealers must reduce positions. Nonbank dealers have no ordinary modeled window eligibility.
policy_dilemma: Collateral-looking assets do not make nonbank counterparties eligible; rate or purchase tools cannot erase every private funding constraint.
selection_reason: Accepted: Private haircut-driven cash needs show the hard counterparty boundary; model haircut is zero because no window-eligible collateral is pledged.

title: An effective vaccine permits broader reopening
mechanism: A successful public-health rollout reduces precautionary contact avoidance and work interruptions; pent-up spending returns before service staffing fully catches up.
policy_dilemma: Demand can recover faster than capacity; favorable health news is not a reason for unlimited monetary stimulus.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable reopening brings a genuine demand-versus-capacity sequencing problem; no vaccine-effect magnitude is claimed.

title: A world commodity-price collapse damages farm loans
mechanism: An external export-demand slump lowers crop receipts and collateral values; some indebted farms default even as food input costs ease for consumers.
policy_dilemma: Favorable food disinflation can coexist with lender losses; liquidity cannot recapitalize exposed banks.
selection_reason: Accepted: Opposite consumer-price and financial-loss signals force a demand-versus-capital diagnosis.

title: A federal shutdown interrupts pay and public services
mechanism: An external appropriation lapse delays household cash receipt and stops some government services; reopening restores services and releases back pay, but lost work is not recreated.
policy_dilemma: Cushion temporary activity loss without treating back pay as permanent income growth or taking Congress powers.
selection_reason: Accepted: A fiscal interruption with pay timing and service loss gives an identifiable multi-quarter demand/supply puzzle.

title: Hurricane destroys housing before rebuilding starts
mechanism: Storm damage displaces households and interrupts work; later rebuilding raises materials demand while usable housing remains scarce. Capital destruction is not directly modeled.
policy_dilemma: Separate a supply interruption from the rebuilding demand pulse; easier rates cannot restore homes.
selection_reason: Accepted: Housing loss followed by rebuilding gives opposite activity signals across quarters and a clear limit to monetary tools.

title: An external immigration decision expands working-age arrivals
mechanism: A nonmonetary immigration change raises available labor and adds household demand; job matching and housing determine which effect reaches firms first.
policy_dilemma: More workers and more consumers arrive together; do not presume the net inflation effect is fixed.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable labor supply with concurrent demand requires diagnosis and preserves the Chair immigration-policy limit.

title: Warehouse automation improves output but displaces tasks
mechanism: A commercial automation rollout lowers handling costs while some workers need new skills; temporary mismatch raises the structural unemployment reference before retraining catches up.
policy_dilemma: Support employment without trying to reverse a productivity gain or inflate away a skills mismatch.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable productive capacity with temporary mismatch tests the difference between cyclical demand and structural adjustment.

title: Wildfire smoke closes schools and outdoor businesses
mechanism: Smoke forces school and work closures far beyond burned land; caregivers miss work and leisure spending falls until air clears.
policy_dilemma: Support weak spending without assuming a rate cut can remove health-related supply constraints.
selection_reason: Accepted: Combines labor availability and lost services demand through smoke rather than direct asset destruction.

title: A bumper grain harvest lowers food and feed costs
mechanism: Mild growing temperatures and unusually low crop disease produce a larger harvest, lowering feed costs. Consumers gain purchasing power while some producers receive less revenue.
policy_dilemma: Stronger consumption during disinflation need not signal excessive demand.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable supply and household purchasing power provide a noncrisis food episode; magnitudes are authored.

title: New semiconductor capacity relieves shortages
mechanism: Qualified new chip production supplies constrained assembly lines; goods availability improves and unit costs fall, though capital orders associated with construction normalize.
policy_dilemma: Faster output during goods disinflation may reflect supply relief rather than excess demand.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable intermediate-input relief connects an identifiable capacity expansion to the existing supply field.

title: Congress authorizes a one-time household rebate
mechanism: An externally legislated payment raises household cash balances; some is spent and some saved or used to repay debt, so the demand pulse fades.
policy_dilemma: More spending may lift activity and inflation; the Chair cannot authorize or redirect the payment.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable household cash relief creates a finite demand pulse and a clear fiscal-versus-monetary boundary.

title: Foreign wholesale lenders withdraw dollar funding from banks
mechanism: External lenders decline to roll dollar claims on trade-financing institutions; some affected U.S. depository counterparties are eligible, while others are not. Funding shortages reduce trade activity.
policy_dilemma: Target secured support only to the eligible bank share, without promising direct dollar loans to foreign firms.
selection_reason: Accepted: Mixed eligibility and working-capital demand create a distinct partial-coverage dilemma; shares are fictional aggregate design.

title: A battery-manufacturing process cuts material use
mechanism: A validated production process uses fewer costly materials per battery; equipment purchases precede cheaper storage and vehicle components. The technological gain is a fictional event.
policy_dilemma: Initial investment demand can precede favorable supply; do not assume lower goods prices imply recession.
selection_reason: Accepted: A favorable manufactured-input efficiency gain offers a clear adoption-before-cost-relief sequence.

title: Large employers offer unexpected early-retirement buyouts
mechanism: Private buyout offers induce experienced workers to leave sooner; payouts briefly support spending while reduced skill availability raises service costs. Labor-force exit is not unemployment.
policy_dilemma: Temporary cash demand and lower labor capacity can coexist despite weak headcount growth.
selection_reason: Accepted: A concrete voluntary-exit trigger avoids presenting slow demographic aging as a surprise and highlights missing participation accounting.

title: Bad corporate earnings news reduces equity wealth
mechanism: Unexpected earnings disappointments lower equity valuations independently of the player policy; exposed households trim consumption and some firms postpone investment.
policy_dilemma: Support real demand without promising to restore stock prices or conflating wealth losses with eligible funding needs.
selection_reason: Accepted: Separates a policy-independent valuation and spending shock from the selected banking funding run.

title: Floodwater shuts an industrial production cluster
mechanism: Inundated plants lose operating days and usable inventories; cleanup restores production before replacement orders fully subside. The profile represents flows, not damaged capital stocks.
policy_dilemma: Distinguish lost production from cleanup orders; late tightening may arrive as bottlenecks clear.
selection_reason: Accepted: Production interruption and subsequent replacement demand create a concrete timing problem.

title: Mortgage audits reveal unenforceable collateral liens
mechanism: An audit finds legal defects in a pool of mortgage liens, reducing expected recovery values even where households keep paying; lenders recognize impairment and tighten underwriting.
policy_dilemma: Borrower cash flow and collateral enforceability differ; the Chair cannot repair legal liens or create equity.
selection_reason: Accepted: A collateral-recovery loss differs from fabricated corporate income and from unavailable pledge documentation in a funding bridge.

title: Post-viral illness reduces available work hours
mechanism: Persistent symptoms after an outbreak limit available work hours and increase caregiving needs; the profile slows capacity growth without equating labor-force exit to unemployment.
policy_dilemma: Potential supply may weaken even when measured unemployment is low; stimulus cannot cure lost work capacity.
selection_reason: Accepted: A persistent health/labor channel tests low unemployment alongside constrained supply; longer-run effects remain outside the profile.

title: Private investors recapitalize troubled banks
mechanism: External shareholders supply loss-absorbing equity and restore confidence in new lending. The existing model can taper new credit pressure but cannot subtract old solvency impairment; relief is conditional.
policy_dilemma: Recognize private capital repair without presenting ordinary Fed liquidity as recapitalization or deleting existing losses.
selection_reason: Accepted: Conditional favorable private repair tests the policy boundary; its true capital accounting is explicitly outside the existing fields.

title: Private depositors commit stable term funding
mechanism: External depositors commit longer-term balances after a scare, so residual bank funding needs taper. This is relief relative to continuing stress, not a negative funding impulse or capital repair.
policy_dilemma: Unwind temporary support as private funding returns; outstanding loans still repay gradually and existing impairment remains.
selection_reason: Accepted: Conditional favorable normalization tests an orderly liquidity unwind without fabricating negative needs or deleting losses.

title: External security news triggers precautionary saving
mechanism: Households build cash buffers after a security scare, postponing discretionary purchases despite unchanged current wages; some spending returns when perceived risks recede.
policy_dilemma: Ease enough to cushion demand while avoiding an unconditional promise that ignores a confidence rebound.
selection_reason: Accepted: A reversible preference for cash is different from lost supply or insolvent lenders.

title: A ceasefire restores direct shipping routes
mechanism: A credible external ceasefire restores safer direct routes; freight capacity is released and delayed cargo arrives before inventory ordering fully normalizes.
policy_dilemma: Do not confuse falling freight costs or arriving cargo with a permanent collapse in demand.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable security resolution adds disinflation plus inventory payback rather than another adverse transport crisis.

title: Shale drilling becomes more productive
mechanism: A commercially deployed drilling improvement yields more oil per crew and lowers supply costs; producers increase output while some high-cost investments become less attractive.
policy_dilemma: Accommodate genuine cost relief without mistaking faster real activity for excessive demand.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable production efficiency contrasts with an oil-demand slump and offers a capacity-led expansion.

title: New childcare capacity releases parental work hours
mechanism: Privately financed centers open after a construction backlog clears, allowing more parents to work; labor availability expands before household spending fully adjusts.
policy_dilemma: Stronger activity with reduced staffing pressure can be supply recovery rather than overheating.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable care capacity improves labor availability without treating participation gains as a mechanical unemployment reduction.

title: Customs digitization clears a goods backlog
mechanism: An external administrative upgrade releases delayed inputs and reduces border processing time; backlog fulfillment briefly supports orders while unit transport costs fall.
policy_dilemma: Cost relief and faster deliveries can strengthen output without broad overheating.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable border efficiency adds a concrete cost-relief/rebound path; the rollout magnitude is not sourced.

title: Foreign income recovery revives inbound tourism
mechanism: Higher incomes in major visitor markets increase domestic hotel, restaurant and transport demand; service staffing responds more slowly than bookings.
policy_dilemma: Favorable export-services demand can strain capacity; monetary easing is not automatically appropriate.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable demand comes from external customers. Its net national scale is an author assumption.

title: Generic medicine production recovers
mechanism: Replacement manufacturing restores scarce essential medicines, reducing treatment interruptions and expensive substitutions; patient demand for deferred care rises afterward.
policy_dilemma: Separate favorable medical cost relief from a temporary catch-up in care spending.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable restoration gives cost relief and delayed demand while respecting that the Chair cannot manufacture medicines.

title: Mild winter extends the construction season
mechanism: An unexpectedly workable winter allows projects to progress and reduces weather delays; activity rises without the usual shortage pressure, then seasonal effects fade.
policy_dilemma: Do not mistake faster building with lower costs for pure overheating.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable weather adds supply relief alongside construction spending; the sign is an authored inference.

title: External credential reform admits already trained professionals
mechanism: A nonmonetary licensing reform lets qualified professionals enter previously restricted jobs, reducing mismatch and service staffing costs while recognition processes phase in.
policy_dilemma: Improved matching is not demand stimulus; avoid unnecessary restraint against expanding service capacity.
selection_reason: Accepted: Favorable access to existing skills is distinct from migration volume or new training; the structural reference resets explicitly.

title: New renewable plants clear a grid connection backlog
mechanism: Previously built generation becomes deliverable after external transmission work finishes, reducing marginal power costs and releasing industrial production bottlenecks.
policy_dilemma: Lower inflation with stronger output may justify less restraint, not automatic rate cuts.
selection_reason: Accepted: A favorable supply completion uses sunk capacity rather than another commodity-price collapse.

title: A bank cannot complete collateral documentation in time
mechanism: A solvent bank loses short-term private funding before loan-pledge records are usable; eligible collateral is initially scarce and improves after documentation finishes. No player waiver exists.
policy_dilemma: Even a sound eligible bank cannot borrow beyond usable pledged collateral; wait for verified capacity rather than promising an exemption.
selection_reason: Excluded: a strong collateral-only boundary, but it adds less causal breadth than the accepted bank payments and dollar-funding cases.

title: A foreign sovereign restructures bank-held debt
mechanism: An external sovereign restructuring reduces recovery values on exposed debt, impairing creditors and tightening lending; domestic monetary policy cannot reverse the legal haircut.
policy_dilemma: Funding support and sovereign credit loss are different; no player power recapitalizes foreign creditors.
selection_reason: Excluded: strong capital distinction, but international sovereign exposures and foreign/domestic spillovers are not explicit.

title: External firms announce a data-center investment boom
mechanism: Large private investment commitments raise orders for construction and computing equipment before any verified increase in economy-wide productivity.
policy_dilemma: Do not label an investment-demand boom as costless supply expansion.
selection_reason: Excluded: strong model fit and recognizability, but the selected AI diffusion episode already includes the more demanding investment-versus-productivity sequence.

title: A foreign export restriction limits a critical mineral
mechanism: An overseas producer restricts a specialized mineral needed for electronics and machinery; alternate supply takes time despite available consumer demand.
policy_dilemma: Demand restraint cannot supply the missing input, though it may contain spillover inflation.
selection_reason: Excluded: distinct input specificity, but the selected fertilizer restriction and chip event cover stronger recognizable examples.

title: Factories adopt a lower-energy production process
mechanism: A commercially proven process reduces fuel use per unit of output; installation spending precedes lower operating costs and modest capacity gains.
policy_dilemma: Initial equipment demand can tighten conditions before lower costs arrive.
selection_reason: Excluded: credible favorable sequencing, but the selected AI and drilling productivity events provide more recognizable versions.

title: LNG export terminals begin drawing domestic gas
mechanism: New export capacity connects domestic gas to foreign buyers; export investment supports activity while household and factory fuel costs face upward pressure.
policy_dilemma: Export-driven demand and domestic energy prices rise together; the Chair cannot ban exports.
selection_reason: Excluded: a useful export-versus-bills conflict, but regional gas pricing and export accounts are compressed too heavily for the first 50.

title: Contamination shuts a specialized chip fabrication line
mechanism: A contamination event removes qualified chip supply for certain assemblies; firms cannot immediately substitute designs, and output restarts after requalification.
policy_dilemma: Higher goods costs reflect unavailable inputs, not a reason to promise instant monetary recovery.
selection_reason: Excluded: credible adverse chip bottleneck, but the selected capacity expansion and fertilizer restriction provide greater sign and sector variety.

title: Investors redeem a prime money-market fund
mechanism: A cash-management fund faces redemptions while holding less-liquid private paper, forcing sales and reducing corporate short-term funding; the fund has no ordinary bank-window access.
policy_dilemma: Do not confuse redeemable fund shares with insured bank deposits or invent nonbank eligibility.
selection_reason: Excluded: genuine redemption transformation, but the dealer selection makes the ineligible-counterparty boundary with a stronger collateral story.

title: A trade dispute ends with a signed agreement
mechanism: An external agreement reduces tariff uncertainty and releases postponed investment and sourcing plans; direct cost relief follows later implementation.
policy_dilemma: Investment demand may return before supply savings; retain conditional rather than unconditional guidance.
selection_reason: Excluded: credible favorable uncertainty resolution, but customs efficiency gives a more concrete initial supply change.

title: Earthquake breaks a specialized supplier network
mechanism: Damaged supplier facilities interrupt otherwise intact assembly plants; firms substitute inputs and restart unevenly. The model cannot represent network topology.
policy_dilemma: Rates can support spending but cannot replace the missing intermediate components.
selection_reason: Excluded: supplier-network propagation is distinctive, but industrial flooding already covers the clearer aggregate interruption-and-restart decision.

title: Errors in deployed AI create widespread rework
mechanism: Firms discover costly mistakes in automated output and temporarily increase human review, reducing effective productivity and delaying completed services.
policy_dilemma: A technology setback can look like stronger hiring demand while usable output slows.
selection_reason: Excluded: a distinct quality-adjustment story, but the macro impact and error prevalence are authored conjectures rather than observed channel estimates.

title: Used-vehicle supply normalizes below lease residual forecasts
mechanism: Unexpectedly abundant used vehicles lower resale values below previously contracted lease assumptions, impairing lessor portfolios while buyers enjoy cheaper cars.
policy_dilemma: Cheaper goods and financial losses coexist; policy cannot rewrite lease residual guarantees.
selection_reason: Excluded: an appealing goods-price/credit conflict, but residual-value guarantees and lessor ownership are absent from the model.

title: Corporate commercial-paper buyers stop rolling maturities
mechanism: Investors stop refinancing sound firms short-term paper after confidence news; issuers cut orders to conserve cash while banks provide only part of the alternative financing.
policy_dilemma: Ordinary secured bank lending cannot be redirected into a fictional direct corporate rescue.
selection_reason: Excluded: maturity rollover differs from fund redemption, but selected funding cases already span full, partial and zero eligibility.

title: Port terminal software failure blocks cargo release
mechanism: A logistics software failure prevents terminal operators from locating and releasing containers; emergency manual processing is slower until records are restored.
policy_dilemma: Liquidity cannot restore cargo records; react to duration rather than a single price spike.
selection_reason: Excluded: an operational port constraint is distinct, but pipeline and broad cloud events already cover clearer cyber/supply tradeoffs.

title: A foreign parent recalls subsidiary dollar funding
mechanism: External home-country restrictions prompt a foreign parent to recall intercompany dollar loans; affected U.S. eligible branches can seek secured support, unlike other group companies.
policy_dilemma: Check the actual local borrower and collateral rather than treating a banking group as uniformly eligible.
selection_reason: Excluded: legal-entity differentiation is real, but the selected wholesale dollar squeeze supplies the clearer mixed-eligibility experience.

title: Foreign LNG supply expansion lowers import competition
mechanism: New overseas liquefaction supply reduces competition among buyers for U.S. gas cargoes; domestic costs ease while export-sector revenue softens.
policy_dilemma: Lower bills coexist with weaker exporter demand; distinguish favorable supply from a global recession.
selection_reason: Excluded: opposite sectoral effects are useful, but the game lacks separate exporter and household accounts.

title: Reservoir drought forces industrial water rationing
mechanism: Low freshwater availability limits cooling and processing at water-intensive plants; production shifts to substitute facilities while rainfall remains uncertain.
policy_dilemma: Additional demand may bid up constrained output rather than restore industrial water.
selection_reason: Excluded: useful water-input distinction, but a national aggregate effect depends heavily on unmodeled plant composition.

title: Safety inspections remove nuclear generation
mechanism: An equipment finding takes several reactors offline; utilities use higher-cost replacement generation until inspections and repairs finish.
policy_dilemma: Do not assume monetary restraint can substitute for missing baseload power.
selection_reason: Excluded: fuel substitution is distinctive, but selected electricity-capacity relief and gas scarcity already cover stronger energy tradeoffs.

title: Fiscal authorities release strategic oil stocks
mechanism: A legislated stock release adds near-term market supply without creating new production; future replenishment can partly reverse the benefit.
policy_dilemma: Consider temporary cost relief while recognizing reserve release is not a Fed decision.
selection_reason: Excluded: recognizable favorable relief, but reserve accounting and replenishment are absent and shale efficiency adds a cleaner upside.

title: Ice accumulation breaks local electricity distribution
mechanism: Ice damages wires and blocks crews, stopping shops and factories even where generation remains available; repairs release orders later.
policy_dilemma: Treat physical distribution failure differently from a broad credit shortage.
selection_reason: Excluded: distribution damage is real, but the selected energy outages offer richer multi-quarter cost and demand tensions.

title: School outbreaks increase caregiver absences
mechanism: Outbreak-related classroom closures force parents to miss paid work even when those parents are healthy; reopened classrooms restore hours.
policy_dilemma: A caregiver labor constraint is not solved by lower borrowing costs.
selection_reason: Excluded: distinct transmission through healthy caregivers, but wildfire smoke and childcare recovery selections already span this constraint.

title: Businesses rebuild unusually lean inventories
mechanism: Firms raise orders to restore stock buffers after an external supply scare; inventory investment rises before final sales, then orders normalize.
policy_dilemma: Do not extrapolate stock rebuilding as permanent customer demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: genuine inventory investment, but the game lacks the stocks needed to explain the correction clearly.

title: Commodity price volatility triggers trader margin calls
mechanism: An external commodity-price jump requires leveraged nonbank traders to post cash before physical-sale receipts arrive; liquidity needs may occur even on hedged positions.
policy_dilemma: A cash call is not automatically a loss, and ordinary bank-window access does not extend to traders.
selection_reason: Excluded: hedging cash timing adds variety, but margin and offsetting derivative positions need explicit accounts for a faithful experience.

title: A proven seed variety raises harvest reliability
mechanism: Commercial adoption of a verified drought-tolerant variety reduces crop losses and unit costs; seed purchases arrive before improved yields.
policy_dilemma: Input spending can rise before favorable supply appears; avoid assuming instantaneous productivity.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable agricultural technology is plausible, but cited evidence supports input/yield channels rather than this hypothetical seed result.

title: Transformer shortages delay power restoration
mechanism: A shortage of specialized transformers slows grid repair and new connections, prolonging expensive backup power and delaying business openings.
policy_dilemma: Demand support cannot quickly produce specialized grid hardware.
selection_reason: Excluded: repair-stock and connection constraints are weakly represented, despite the useful longer duration.

title: Hospitals lose beds during an admission surge
mechanism: A sudden admission surge crowds out scheduled care and diverts scarce staff; deferred treatments return when hospital capacity normalizes.
policy_dilemma: Medical spending weakness during rationing is not necessarily weak demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: crowding-out of medical services is distinctive, but hospital queues and rationing are not separate model states.

title: A court decision releases workers from restrictive job covenants
mechanism: In this hypothetical external ruling, workers can switch employers more freely, improving match quality while firms incur temporary recruiting and handover costs.
policy_dilemma: Improved matching can reduce structural frictions even as turnover temporarily rises.
selection_reason: Excluded: a distinct mobility mechanism, but an early primary study reports null effects; positive matching gains remain a fictional condition and mobility is unmodeled.

title: Pollinator losses reduce fruit and nut yields
mechanism: A disease-driven loss of managed and wild pollinators reduces output in dependent crops, while grains are less affected; replacement colonies require time.
policy_dilemma: Relative food prices can rise without a broad demand boom.
selection_reason: Excluded: genuine biological distinction, but crop-level substitution and national weight are not modeled.

title: Delayed import deliveries arrive all at once
mechanism: Previously delayed shipments arrive together, creating excess retail inventories; merchants discount and reduce new orders despite steady final demand.
policy_dilemma: Goods disinflation can coexist with falling factory orders; avoid confusing inventory correction with household collapse.
selection_reason: Excluded: inventory timing gives real variety, but the game cannot separate inventory investment from final demand.

title: A commuter transit shutdown prevents workers reaching jobs
mechanism: A safety-related transit closure removes reliable access to workplaces; lost hours and substitute travel costs persist until service restarts.
policy_dilemma: Transport-constrained labor supply is not repaired by lower interest rates.
selection_reason: Excluded: physical access is a distinct labor channel, but local travel substitutions dominate the aggregate result.

title: Crypto collateral collapses at exposed lenders
mechanism: An external confidence break lowers volatile crypto collateral values, causing borrower defaults and creditor impairment; most directly exposed nonbanks have no ordinary bank-window claim.
policy_dilemma: Do not equate falling token prices with an eligible funding shortage or promise investor loss protection.
selection_reason: Excluded: recognizable collateral loss, but institutional crypto exposures and liquidation values would require richer accounts.

title: Foreign conflict accelerates external defense procurement
mechanism: The fiscal authority advances purchases of military equipment from domestic firms; orders lift demand before manufacturers expand capacity.
policy_dilemma: Higher government demand can tighten resources, but the Chair cannot cancel procurement or fund the military.
selection_reason: Excluded: a concrete fiscal demand concept, but defense-specific procurement evidence and sector capacity require further primary-source review.

title: Customers rush to redeem a nonbank payment wallet
mechanism: Confidence news causes simultaneous withdrawals from a wallet provider while backing assets are less liquid; suppliers and users delay transactions. Ordinary bank eligibility remains zero.
policy_dilemma: Do not promise deposit insurance or a direct Fed bailout of a payment app.
selection_reason: Excluded: familiar platform run but legal backing and customer claims are central missing mechanics.

title: Private creditors agree an orderly borrower debt workout
mechanism: External creditors extend maturities and accept negotiated losses, reducing new lending stress and permitting viable borrowers to resume orders. Existing model impairment cannot be written down by a negative shock.
policy_dilemma: Orderly private resolution may support demand, but do not claim Fed rates can choose creditor losses or make insolvent borrowers sound.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable private resolution is distinct from new shareholder equity, but neither debt seniority nor loss allocation exists in the game.

title: Private creditors settle distressed household debts
mechanism: Private negotiated settlements reduce future household payments but impose creditor losses; some released cash supports consumption while lending may tighten elsewhere.
policy_dilemma: Demand relief and lender impairment are different channels; the Chair cannot order debt cancellation.
selection_reason: Excluded: a genuine cash-flow/capital tradeoff, but distribution and creditor recovery values are compressed too much.

title: External military mobilization removes reservists from civilian work
mechanism: A foreign security emergency prompts the government to mobilize civilian reservists, reducing available hours in affected occupations while defense spending supports demand.
policy_dilemma: Lower civilian capacity and fiscal demand can conflict; the Chair cannot control military staffing.
selection_reason: Excluded: military staffing is an identifiable external labor withdrawal, but cited labor channels do not estimate mobilization and the model lacks civilian/military sectors.

title: Uninsured disaster losses impair property-backed loans
mechanism: Physical damage outside insurance coverage removes collateral and borrower income, generating credit losses after emergency operations end. Rebuilding demand does not automatically restore lender recovery.
policy_dilemma: Do not assume insured-style cash payouts or eligible liquidity can erase destroyed collateral.
selection_reason: Excluded: insurance coverage changes the financial aftermath, but it overlaps the selected hurricane damage story and lacks explicit collateral stocks.

title: Telehealth reduces travel and scheduling barriers
mechanism: An external commercial rollout enables more suitable appointments remotely, saving travel time and expanding access; not every examination can move online.
policy_dilemma: Determine whether greater service use reflects productive capacity or excess demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable remote-service efficiency is plausible, but these references support attendance/supply channels rather than a measured telehealth macro effect.

title: A foreign recession cuts U.S. export orders
mechanism: A downturn abroad reduces orders for domestic manufactured goods and services, lowering activity without an initial U.S. production bottleneck.
policy_dilemma: Domestic easing may cushion lost external demand but cannot revive foreign customers by decree.
selection_reason: Excluded: strong model fit but a conventional demand response, with less tool-choice tension than selected trade supply events.

title: An unusually large apprenticeship cohort becomes qualified
mechanism: A previously funded training cohort completes certification and fills skilled vacancies; output per worker and job matching improve without new migration.
policy_dilemma: More employment and lower scarcity costs may reflect training supply rather than excess demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable skill supply is distinct, but credential recognition is quicker to explain and creates a clearer institutional boundary.

title: A legislated student-loan payment pause ends
mechanism: An external statutory payment resumption diverts some household cash from consumption to debt service; spending weakness depends on savings and borrower income.
policy_dilemma: Cushion weak demand without claiming authority to forgive or suspend those debts.
selection_reason: Excluded: concrete cash-flow reversal, but borrower incidence is absent and the model offers a fairly routine demand response.

title: Hail destroys vehicles and accelerates replacements
mechanism: Vehicle damage brings forward household replacement purchases and repair work, then leaves a payback in later auto demand; the loss itself is not new output.
policy_dilemma: Decide whether a short replacement surge warrants persistent restraint.
selection_reason: Excluded: the demand payback is useful, but aggregate scale is narrow and weaker than the selected rebuilding episode.

title: Refineries lose access to a critical catalyst
mechanism: A specialty-chemical supplier interruption reduces refinery throughput even with ample crude; fuel margins rise until alternative catalyst supply qualifies.
policy_dilemma: A crude-price decline need not mean retail fuel inflation is resolved.
selection_reason: Excluded: strong input distinction but low recognizability and overlap with the selected chip and pipeline bottlenecks.

title: Foreign buyers reopen a restricted farm-export market
mechanism: An external market reopening increases export orders and farm income but diverts some food from domestic buyers; supply expands only after planting.
policy_dilemma: Export-led activity can raise domestic food prices; the Chair cannot allocate harvests.
selection_reason: Excluded: real trade allocation tension, but separate domestic/export food markets are absent.

title: Rail dispute restricts coal deliveries to utilities
mechanism: Coal deliveries slow while inventories decline, forcing electricity producers to switch fuels or pay for alternate transport; settlement restores flows.
policy_dilemma: Treat energy-input scarcity rather than aggregate overheating as the initial cause.
selection_reason: Excluded: energy fuel switching is concrete, but a rail bottleneck is less distinctive than the selected pipeline interruption.

title: Sanitation failures close large food-processing lines
mechanism: A contamination finding removes processing capacity and recalls finished food; safe replacement production restores supply after inspections.
policy_dilemma: Tighter demand cannot substitute for food-safety repair, though secondary inflation pressure may matter.
selection_reason: Excluded: a concrete processing interruption, but drug-manufacturing and egg-supply selections already give clearer safety/biological constraints.

title: New container ships expand freight capacity
mechanism: Previously ordered vessels are delivered and usable shipping slots increase, reducing freight costs; some operator earnings weaken as backlogs clear.
policy_dilemma: Rising goods availability with disinflation need not require broad easing.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable capital completion is useful, but sea-lane reopening offers a richer timing and inventory problem.

title: Low reservoir inflows reduce hydropower output
mechanism: Low inflows reduce cheap hydropower generation, raising reliance on purchased thermal power; rain eventually restores part of the output.
policy_dilemma: Support spending carefully when electricity capacity rather than credit is scarce.
selection_reason: Excluded: a physical generation channel, but the selected weather and gas events cover a clearer national policy problem.

title: Marine insurers reprice oil-cargo coverage
mechanism: Insurers withdraw cheap cover after external security news, raising the delivered cost of otherwise available crude and causing routing changes.
policy_dilemma: Do not treat an insurance-and-transport premium as evidence of stronger oil consumption.
selection_reason: Excluded: insurance costs differ from physical oil cuts, but the selected maritime and oil events span the principal dilemma more clearly.

title: A damaged rail bridge closes a freight corridor
mechanism: An engineering inspection closes a key bridge, diverting bulk freight to more expensive transport until repairs pass safety checks.
policy_dilemma: Lower rates cannot restore safe capacity; a short cost shock may fade before policy transmission peaks.
selection_reason: Excluded: route substitution is credible, but the selected sea-route events are more recognizable and broadly consequential.

title: Manufacturing defects interrupt sterile injectable supply
mechanism: Quality failures at a concentrated supplier delay procedures and force costly substitute drugs; qualified alternative production comes online later.
policy_dilemma: Do not attribute higher medical costs to broad spending excess or promise rate cuts will fix manufacturing quality.
selection_reason: Excluded: safety-driven supply loss is concrete, but the selected favorable generic recovery covers the same manufacturing bottleneck more usefully.

title: Truck fuel deliveries are rationed
mechanism: A supplier distribution failure limits diesel availability for truck fleets; shipments compete for fuel and inventories thin before normal deliveries return.
policy_dilemma: Higher freight prices may reflect unavailable inputs, not too much consumer spending.
selection_reason: Excluded: transport-specific propagation is real, but it duplicates much of the selected fuel pipeline episode.

title: A safe low-cost feed substitute reaches livestock farms
mechanism: A commercially validated substitute lowers livestock feed costs while existing grain demand softens; meat supply benefits gradually rather than immediately.
policy_dilemma: Falling food costs may coexist with weaker crop incomes; avoid reading one sector as the whole economy.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable substitution is author inference, and the model cannot separate livestock benefits from grain-producer losses.

title: Securitization delays leave warehouse loans unfunded
mechanism: A private securitization market interruption delays loan takeout, leaving originators with expiring warehouse financing; only the eligible bank portion can use pledged assets for ordinary support.
policy_dilemma: A funding bridge must respect collateral and borrower status; it cannot validate the underlying loans.
selection_reason: Excluded: contractual takeout risk is useful but obscure, and warehouse assets and securitization are not separately recorded.

title: Trade insurers withdraw supplier payment cover
mechanism: Private insurers withdraw receivables coverage after counterparty news, so exporters require cash up front; working-capital costs rise and orders are delayed.
policy_dilemma: Funding strain and counterparty losses require different responses; ordinary Fed lending cannot directly insure exports.
selection_reason: Excluded: contractual trade-credit constraints are distinctive but insurance and exporter balance sheets are unmodeled.

title: Accessible job redesign permits disabled workers to enter
mechanism: Commercial employers introduce suitable flexible and accessible roles, enabling some previously excluded workers to supply hours; adaptation spending comes before capacity gains.
policy_dilemma: Greater work access is favorable supply, not evidence that disability itself has vanished.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable work redesign is distinct from a cure, but direct participation and disability transitions are missing.

title: A clearinghouse calls extra cash from member banks
mechanism: External volatility prompts a clearinghouse to demand more cash from eligible member banks; sound banks temporarily use pledged assets while positions are settled.
policy_dilemma: Eligible liquidity can bridge cash demands but cannot cancel clearing margins or absorb trading losses.
selection_reason: Excluded: an institutional margin bridge differs from nonbank commodity hedges, but intraday obligations are heavily compressed into quarterly flows.

title: An employer campus move strands specialized workers
mechanism: A private relocation separates skilled workers from available matching jobs; some cannot move immediately because of housing constraints, increasing mismatch until reemployment.
policy_dilemma: Employment weakness can be partly structural; stimulus cannot instantly relocate people or supply housing.
selection_reason: Excluded: spatial skills mismatch is real, but the parent model lacks separate regions and local vacancies.

title: Citrus greening damages established orchards
mechanism: Plant disease lowers juice yields and damages long-lived trees, increasing unit costs; immediate replanting cannot restore mature production.
policy_dilemma: Persistent agricultural capacity loss should not be diagnosed as excess consumer demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: orchard capital and multi-year recovery do not fit a one-to-four-quarter episode well.

title: A major foreign buyer defaults on trade receivables
mechanism: An external customer default removes expected cash receipts and damages exporter loans; healthy demand elsewhere cannot instantly replace the realized receivable loss.
policy_dilemma: Eligible bank cash support may address related timing, but it does not erase the customer default.
selection_reason: Excluded: buyer default differs from insurance withdrawal, but trade receivable ownership and recovery are not separate accounts.

title: A court judgment imposes large liabilities on indebted firms
mechanism: An external legal judgment adds liabilities beyond the available assets of some firms, causing restructuring and lender impairment; productive equipment may remain intact.
policy_dilemma: Intact production capacity does not imply financial solvency; the Chair cannot cancel a legal judgment.
selection_reason: Excluded: legal liabilities create a distinct cause of insolvency, but court recovery and balance-sheet priorities need stronger direct evidence.

title: Home-care capacity falls after provider exits
mechanism: Independent care providers close after operating losses, leaving relatives to reduce market work to care for adults; alternative providers restore only part of those hours.
policy_dilemma: A care bottleneck can shrink measured labor supply without a corresponding unemployment jump.
selection_reason: Excluded: adult-care obligations are distinct from childcare, but participation and unpaid care are not explicit model states.

title: A catastrophe creates large insurer cash-payment obligations
mechanism: A solvent insurer must pay claims before invested assets can be sold normally; liquidity pressure causes asset sales. The insurer is not an eligible ordinary bank borrower.
policy_dilemma: Avoid treating claim-payment timing as proof of insolvency or granting the insurer invented window access.
selection_reason: Excluded: cash timing is genuinely different from claim underreserving, but insurance balance sheets and payouts are not modeled.

title: An insurer discovers long-tail claim underreserving
mechanism: An actuarial revision raises expected liabilities beyond previously reserved amounts, reducing insurer capital and increasing risk premiums; no immediate redemption run is assumed.
policy_dilemma: A liability valuation loss is not solved by secured cash and the Chair cannot recapitalize the insurer.
selection_reason: Excluded: solvency without a cash run is valuable, but long-tail insurance liabilities and regulation are absent.

title: A leveraged acquisition sponsor fails to supply promised equity
mechanism: An external sponsor failure removes promised capital for indebted acquired firms, causing restructurings and losses for leveraged-loan holders; a cash bridge cannot replace missing equity.
policy_dilemma: Separate refinancing pressure from an unsustainable capital structure.
selection_reason: Excluded: missing sponsor equity is distinct, but acquisition guarantees and lender recovery priorities are not recorded.

title: A certification exam cancellation delays workforce entry
mechanism: An external administrative failure postpones qualifying exams, leaving trained entrants unable to fill regulated vacancies until a new session is held.
policy_dilemma: Demand support cannot legally qualify workers; distinguish delayed entry from falling job demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: genuinely administrative labor supply, but scale is narrow and similar aggregate outcomes are covered by credential reform.

title: Algal toxins close a major shellfish fishery
mechanism: A marine heatwave supports toxic blooms and closes harvesting; seafood supply and coastal incomes fall until testing permits reopening.
policy_dilemma: Supply scarcity and lost local income coexist; monetary tools cannot certify safe harvests.
selection_reason: Excluded: compelling local effects, but the national one-sector reduction is small and less legible than selected food shocks.

title: A critical medical-device recall restricts procedures
mechanism: A safety recall removes a widely used device from service; hospitals postpone procedures or use costlier equipment until replacements arrive.
policy_dilemma: Higher care prices can arise from safety-constrained supply rather than too much purchasing power.
selection_reason: Excluded: device capacity differs from medicines, but the aggregate policy path resembles the excluded injectable shortage.

title: A water contamination warning closes businesses
mechanism: An external contamination incident prevents food-service and care facilities from using normal water supplies; bottled substitutes and testing increase costs until clearance.
policy_dilemma: Monetary stimulus cannot certify safe water; distinguish public-health shutdowns from falling customer interest.
selection_reason: Excluded: concrete safety closure, but the broad references do not identify its aggregate effect and the model lacks water-service capacity.

title: Private-credit valuations reveal previously hidden borrower losses
mechanism: External audits force delayed markdowns of private loans, reducing fund asset values and willingness to finance new projects; ordinary window eligibility is not assumed.
policy_dilemma: Illiquid valuations and credit loss differ from bank funding stress; avoid inventing a fund bailout.
selection_reason: Excluded: appraisal lag is distinct, but accounting marks and private-fund capital cannot be shown faithfully by one persistent wedge.

title: A cable failure degrades international data service
mechanism: Damage to a major data cable forces traffic onto slower alternatives, disrupting outsourced services and cross-border business coordination until repair.
policy_dilemma: A communications bottleneck can depress activity even when domestic borrowing conditions are unchanged.
selection_reason: Excluded: distinct communications transport, but specific network exposure and domestic scale need stronger evidence.

title: Volcanic ash suspends air cargo and travel
mechanism: Ash makes aviation routes unsafe, stranding high-value components and travelers; rerouting raises cost before flights resume. Ground transport substitutes only partly.
policy_dilemma: Monetary easing cannot reopen airspace; look for persistent rather than transit-timing inflation.
selection_reason: Excluded: primary evidence supports aviation disruptions, but airspace routing and national exposure are less well represented than selected maritime bottlenecks.

title: A major event attracts an unexpected visitor surge
mechanism: An unexpectedly large international audience raises short-lived lodging and hospitality purchases; demand drops after the event even if some visitor infrastructure remains.
policy_dilemma: Do not turn a one-quarter services bottleneck into lasting monetary restraint.
selection_reason: Excluded: concentrated visitor timing is distinct, but foreign tourism revival is the broader and more replay-relevant selection.

title: A successful therapy releases chronic-care work capacity
mechanism: In this hypothetical episode, an effective treatment reduces disabling symptoms and caregiver time; adoption costs precede a modest improvement in available labor hours.
policy_dilemma: Up-front medical spending may rise before productive-capacity gains arrive.
selection_reason: Excluded: the labor channel is supported, but the successful therapy and its economic gain are invented rather than observed.

title: Households shift purchases from goods to experiences
mechanism: A taste change reallocates spending toward services while goods sellers discount excess stocks; total purchasing power need not change. The aggregate profile is only a proxy.
policy_dilemma: Offsetting sector pressures can cancel nationally; avoid assuming every relative-price move is excess total demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: genuinely compositional demand cannot be represented faithfully by one output gap and one supply-pressure state.

title: A cybersecurity standard triggers equipment replacement
mechanism: An externally required security standard causes firms to replace unsupported systems together; capital spending rises initially and then drops after the deadline.
policy_dilemma: A compliance deadline can front-load investment without raising permanent demand growth.
selection_reason: Excluded: a distinct deadline-driven investment cycle, but a mostly one-direction stance decision contributes less replay variety.

title: Rain restores industrial water access
mechanism: Sustained rainfall replenishes reservoirs enough to relax existing processing limits; plants fulfill backlogs and unit costs ease. The weather benefit is conditional on prior scarcity.
policy_dilemma: Allow capacity recovery without confusing backlog fulfillment with unlimited future demand.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable relief is worthwhile, but mild winter supplies a more immediately recognizable weather upside.

title: An aging vehicle cohort reaches replacement age
mechanism: A large privately owned vehicle cohort becomes costly to maintain, bringing replacements forward; purchases later ease after the cohort has been renewed.
policy_dilemma: Temporary replacements may resemble durable-goods overheating; judge persistence before extending restraint.
selection_reason: Excluded: replacement timing is distinct from hail damage, but less unexpected and less policy-rich than the selected demand episodes.

title: A deferred-care backlog is released
mechanism: Hospitals clear a scheduling backlog and households purchase postponed procedures; temporary healthcare spending rises without a new lasting income source.
policy_dilemma: Avoid treating a bounded catch-up as sustained aggregate demand acceleration.
selection_reason: Excluded: recognizable demand catch-up, but vaccine reopening already contains a broader version with stronger supply tension.

title: Foreign entry restrictions reduce inbound travel
mechanism: An external travel-rule change prevents some visitors reaching domestic hotels and attractions; bookings recover after the rule expires.
policy_dilemma: A border-driven services slump is temporary but rate transmission is delayed.
selection_reason: Excluded: different institutional cause from health avoidance, but a similar aggregate demand path and limited replay gain.

title: Coastal evacuation cancels a tourism season
mechanism: Visitors cancel prepaid trips during evacuation warnings; local services lose revenue and some bookings return later even if physical damage is limited.
policy_dilemma: Weigh temporary services weakness against any later catch-up, without promising income transfers.
selection_reason: Excluded: a concrete services demand interruption, but contact-avoidance and tourism-revival selections provide stronger contrasting paths.

title: Storage pests destroy a grain stockpile
mechanism: An infestation removes already harvested grain from usable inventories, tightening supply without changing field yields; alternative stocks arrive later.
policy_dilemma: A stock loss can lift prices while crop data still look strong.
selection_reason: Excluded: primary research supports storage-pest losses, but the game has no usable-grain stock and the national aggregate effect depends on concentration.

title: Refrigerated food inventories spoil during a power failure
mechanism: A refrigeration outage destroys perishable stocks; emergency restocking raises transport and wholesale costs before usable inventories recover.
policy_dilemma: Distinguish replacement purchases from stronger final consumption.
selection_reason: Excluded: inventory spoilage is distinct, but both inventory stocks and food-specific pricing are missing.

title: Tornado destroys a distribution warehouse
mechanism: Stored finished goods disappear rather than being delayed; retailers place replacement orders while manufacturers face a brief inventory shortfall.
policy_dilemma: Replacement orders may look like broad demand strength even though households have lost assets.
selection_reason: Excluded: lost inventories differ from shipping delay, but their stock accounting is absent from the model.

title: External funding cuts interrupt vocational placements
mechanism: A nonmonetary funding lapse cancels final practical placements, delaying a trained cohort entering skilled occupations; restored placements permit later entry.
policy_dilemma: Do not claim monetary easing can replace training grants or supervised work placements.
selection_reason: Excluded: a training-stage cause differs from exam administration, but its policy experience is too similar for the first 50.

title: Large employers relocate staff into tight housing markets
mechanism: Independent corporate relocations raise moving and housing demand in destination cities while old locations lose spending; the proposed aggregate pulse covers transaction activity only.
policy_dilemma: Regional housing pressure can be strong even when national net demand changes little.
selection_reason: Excluded: spatial redistribution dominates; a national one-sector impulse would overstate what the model can represent.

title: A municipality misses expected tax-receipt timing
mechanism: An administrative collection delay leaves a local authority short of cash for payroll despite expected future receipts; private bridge financing becomes more expensive.
policy_dilemma: The Chair cannot finance a municipal payroll directly or substitute monetary tools for tax administration.
selection_reason: Excluded: public cash timing is distinct, but direct local-government financing and its source evidence do not fit the ordinary bank model.

title: Private health insurers reprice coverage after loss reviews
mechanism: A private claim-cost review raises household health premiums, reducing disposable cash. Premiums do not pass one-for-one into measured medical inflation; only the consumption cash-flow channel is profiled.
policy_dilemma: Distinguish a cost repricing from demand overheating and avoid claiming the Chair can fund household premiums.
selection_reason: Excluded: concrete household cash-flow pressure, but medical price measurement and insurer incidence are absent; no direct premium-to-inflation equivalence is assumed.

title: Workers unexpectedly prefer fewer market hours
mechanism: A broad external social preference shift leads households to choose fewer paid hours and more leisure, lowering available capacity without layoffs. Leisure welfare is not measured.
policy_dilemma: Low unemployment may coexist with reduced production potential; demand stimulus cannot supply voluntarily forgone hours.
selection_reason: Excluded: a distinct labor-supply preference, but the game has neither hours choice nor leisure and the surprise trigger is underspecified.

title: Flood recession allows stores to reopen
mechanism: Water recedes and cleanup makes retail districts usable again; services spending resumes before household property losses are recovered.
policy_dilemma: A reopening bounce is not proof that damage has vanished or that maximum stimulus is still needed.
selection_reason: Excluded: recovery is distinct from destruction but overlaps the selected flood episode aftermath.

title: A durable material reduces maintenance shutdowns
mechanism: Commercial adoption of a longer-lived component reduces routine plant downtime and replacement costs; production improves without an equivalent final-demand increase.
policy_dilemma: Higher output alongside lower costs may warrant less restraint, not extra stimulus.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable maintenance efficiency is distinctive, but component lifetime and capital services are not separate game states.

title: An open manufacturing standard reduces integration costs
mechanism: An external industry standard lets previously incompatible equipment communicate, reducing downtime and integration spending while raising effective plant utilization.
policy_dilemma: Stronger utilization may reflect lower frictions rather than new demand requiring restraint.
selection_reason: Excluded: genuine interoperability benefit but low recognizability and no direct estimate of the proposed standard effect.

title: Export windfalls trigger large employee profit-sharing payments
mechanism: Independent foreign orders create contractual profit-sharing payments, transferring corporate cash to employees; spending rises temporarily while firms retain less for investment.
policy_dilemma: A wage-income windfall can boost consumption without expanding productive capacity at the same time.
selection_reason: Excluded: income redistribution differs from fiscal rebates or equity wealth, but the corporate-investment offset is not separate in the model.

title: Local property reassessments raise cash tax bills
mechanism: An external local assessment change raises property-tax payments for some owners, reducing spendable cash; renters and public services may face different later effects.
policy_dilemma: Weak private spending does not give the Chair authority to change local taxes.
selection_reason: Excluded: a concrete nonmonetary cash-flow shock, but the spending/public-service offset needs fiscal detail absent from the reduced form.

title: Frost damages coffee trees rather than one harvest
mechanism: Cold weather damages perennial coffee trees, raising import costs beyond a single crop season; consumers substitute while growers rebuild productive plants.
policy_dilemma: A narrow imported price rise does not necessarily justify broad demand restraint.
selection_reason: Excluded: perennial-tree damage is genuinely different from annual crop drought, but sector weight and recovery horizon are poor fits.

title: Industrial software patents expire
mechanism: Expiration of commercially important rights allows competing suppliers to reduce licensing costs and expand access; firms adjust workflows over time.
policy_dilemma: Lower service prices with better access may be favorable supply, but adoption demand can still rise.
selection_reason: Excluded: favorable legal-cost mechanism is distinct, but intellectual-property pricing is not directly evidenced by these general innovation sources.

title: Landslide cuts access to a major ore mine
mechanism: A buried access corridor prevents ore reaching smelters despite intact reserves; temporary imports raise costs until transport access reopens.
policy_dilemma: Avoid stimulating downstream orders into an unavailable raw-material input.
selection_reason: Excluded: requires a specific concentration assumption and resembles the broader selected trade-input bottlenecks.

title: Navigation interference disrupts precision operations
mechanism: External interference degrades positioning used by farms and freight fleets, increasing manual work and delaying deliveries; alternative systems restore some performance.
policy_dilemma: Demand support cannot restore accurate positioning, and the aggregate effect depends on substitutes.
selection_reason: Excluded: primary evidence supports navigation disruption, but precise transport/farm exposures and substitute positioning systems are outside the game.

title: Drug-resistant infections lengthen hospital care
mechanism: Harder-to-treat infections consume more beds and staff per patient, raising medical resource costs and extending workers time away.
policy_dilemma: Broad demand restraint cannot directly reduce resource requirements per case.
selection_reason: Excluded: primary evidence supports higher care burden, but a healthcare-resource-intensity shock is poorly represented by a single aggregate supply-pressure state.

title: A research breakthrough promises faster commercial optimization
mechanism: A laboratory result prompts investment hopes before commercially useful computation is demonstrated; the authored profile includes equipment demand, not proven productivity.
policy_dilemma: Do not accommodate an assumed supply gain that has not reached production.
selection_reason: Excluded: commercial quantum gains are speculative; low model fit and weak channel specificity outweigh novelty.
